newsitem.title: TURKEY: Twenty-eight dead in Turkish coach crash.
newsitem.headline: Twenty-eight dead in Turkish coach crash.

text.p: Twenty-eight people were killed when a coach crashed into a ditch in eastern Turkey early on Friday, local officials said.
"We believe the bus crashed into the ditch because the driver fell asleep at the wheel," Recep Yazicioglu, governor of eastern Erzincan province, told Reuters.
He said the crash happened at about 5 a.m. (0200 GMT) at Sakaltutan, 20 km (12 miles) west of the town of Erzincan.
Anatolian news agency said 16 people were injured in the accident as the double-decker coach travelled from Ankara to Agri in eastern Turkey. It said three pepople died in hospital.
Several of the casualties, taken to various hospitals in Erzincan and neighbouring Erzurum province, were reported to be badly injured, the private NTV television channel said.
Turkey has one of the worst road traffic death rates in the world. Last Sunday, 18 people died in a motorway pile-up in southern Turkey.
